body:
**Deepak Nitrite**
- India's largest phenol/acetone producer since 2018 (an import-substitution capex). The stock rose more than 100% in CY20 and 135% in six months to Mar 2021 — [Business Standard Mar 2021](https://www.business-standard.com/article/markets/deepak-nitrite-analysts-see-further-upside-despite-135-rally-in-6-months-121030500331_1.html); [BS Aug 2020](https://www.business-standard.com/article/markets/deepak-nitrite-rises-9-hits-52-week-high-stock-up-over-100-in-cy20-120082500603_1.html)
- FY26 net profit ₹550.7 cr against ₹697.4 cr in FY25, earnings falling. Price about ₹1,590 in a ₹1,280–1,898 range, well below its 2021–22 peak — [Upstox/Indmoney page via search](https://upstox.com/stocks/deepak-nitrite-ltd-share-price/INE288B01029) (treat the price as unverified). This is a **post-multibagger derating case**.

**Dixon Technologies**
- Up 125% in CY2024 to October against about 13% for the Sensex. Analysts expected about 91% YoY revenue growth from mobiles and acquisitions — [Business Standard Oct 2024](https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/trent-dixon-ipca-coforge-akzo-nobel-hit-record-highs-rally-up-to-8-124100800610_1.html). I found no source that explicitly attributes this to PLI.

**Motilal Oswal wealth-creation base rates**
- 2016–21: ₹10 lakh split across the top-10 fastest creators grew to ₹1.7 cr. **8 of the top 10 had a market cap below ₹2,000 cr in 2016** (small size is a precondition) — [MOSL WC press](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/article/markets/reliance-industries-largest-wealth-creator-in-2016-21-says-motilal-oswal-121121401678_1.html)
- The fastest creators by period were Lloyds Metals (2018–23, 79% CAGR), Adani Green (2019–24, 118% CAGR) and BSE (2020–25, 124% TR CAGR). The equal-weight top 10 grew from ₹10m to ₹240m over 2020–25 — [MOSL 28th](https://www.motilaloswalgroup.com/Media-Room/Press-Release/-/motilal-oswal-28th-annual-wealth-creation-stu/FS/20499); [MOSL 29th](https://www.motilaloswalgroup.com/Media-Room/Press-Release/-/motilal-oswal-29th-annual-wealth-creation-stu/FS/20685); [MOSL 30th PDF](https://www.motilaloswal.com/content/dam/mofsl-website-adobe/investor-relations/wealth-creation/wc30.pdf)

body:
`insight:rerating-vs-eps` · confidence: single-source

Decomposing the moves [approximate, my arithmetic from public EPS/P/E ranges]: Apple 2003-12 ~110x was ~100% EPS with P/E compression; Apple 2016-23 ~8x was ~half EPS (x2.9, buyback-aided) and half P/E (11x -> 30x); Microsoft 2014-25 ~15x = EPS ~5x x P/E ~2.5x; Costco 2009-26 ~29x = EPS ~7x x P/E ~3.5x; Meta 2022-25 ~9x = EPS ~2.8x x P/E ~3x; Palantir 2022-25 ~35x was mostly multiple (P/S 8.5x -> 137x vs revenue ~2.5x); Tesla 2019-21 ~35x was mostly multiple. Durability followed the mix: EPS-led winners kept compounding or stalled gently; multiple-led winners gave back 36-73% (Palantir, Tesla, Celsius, Enphase) even while still growing. The best risk/reward combos had both engines starting from a depressed multiple (the twin-engine pattern: Apple 2016 at ~10x, Meta 2022 at ~9x, Microsoft 2014 at ~14x). Lesson: estimate what share of the expected return requires the multiple to rise; above ~50% from an already-high multiple, the position is a bet on sentiment and should be sized as such.

- **Links:** `insight:twin-engine`, `case_study:apple-2016-2023-buffett`, `case_study:palantir-2022-2026`, `case_study:costco-2009-2026`
